key_insight: Y6 excitons are not purely Frenkel-like; they contain 20–40% charge-transfer character and move through a delocalization-assisted transport regime that enables rapid interfacial quenching.
engineering_relevance: These results provide a quantitative basis for designing single-component solar cells and interfaces that promote fast exciton extraction and charge generation in non-fullerene acceptor films.
method: Ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy on Y6 films interfaced with hole-transport layers.
Analytical hybrid Frenkel-charge-transfer model to fit quenching dynamics and extract couplings, CT admixture, and system-bath interaction strengths.
Use of the extracted parameters to infer exciton transport and injection length/time scales.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ~1 ps quenching within ~4 nm of the interface, consistent with short-range, delocalization-mediated exciton injection.
watch_item: The model is parameter-rich and inferred mechanisms may depend on film morphology and interface quality, so generalization should be validated across device stacks.
paper_title: Quantitative Analysis of Exciton Composition and Dynamics in Y6 Films for Single-Component Solar Cells
